divergence_analysis.verdict_title: Strong Divergence: Trends Moving in Opposite Directions
divergence_analysis.narrative: A sharp planetary paradox is detected. Over 2001–2025, Marathwada (Drought-Prone Rain Shadow) shows a increasing trend (+2.789 mm/month/decade), while Northeast India (Cherrapunji / Meghalaya Monsoon Belt) exhibits an opposing increasing trend (+10.273 mm/month/decade). Their trajectories are moving in opposite directions.

case_1_monsoon_paradox.title: The Monsoon Paradox: Orographic Deluge vs. Rain-Shadow Drought
case_1_monsoon_paradox.subtitle: Marathwada vs. Northeast India (2001–2025)
case_1_monsoon_paradox.paradox_statement: Despite sharing the same South Asian summer monsoon air mass, why does Northeast India receive up to 1,350+ mm/month causing extreme flash flooding, while Marathwada (just 1,500 km away) suffers persistent agro-meteorological drought (<10 mm/month)?
